title: Approval-triggered reruns: select failed checks from the PR head's statusCheckRollup, keeping only the newest check per job/workflow/event before filtering failures
answers: Why was a job that already passed on a newer attempt still rerun after approval?
Why do approval-triggered reruns of failed checks sometimes take a long time to submit?
Why is the protect job rerun after the other failed jobs?
Where is the logic that picks failed checks to rerun on approval?
body:
Path: .github/workflows/rerun-workflow-run.yml (job rerun-failed-checks, triggered by workflow_run after approval) queries the triggering head SHA's paginated statusCheckRollup via GraphQL and produces the "<run databaseId> <job name>" rows that get passed to `gh run rerun --failed`.
Rule: Dedupe before filtering. Keep only CheckRun nodes whose checkSuite.app.slug is github-actions, group by [name, workflow name, event], keep max_by(startedAt) per group, and only then apply the COMPLETED+FAILURE, rerun/protect, and <=60s duration filters. Use workflowRun.databaseId directly as the run id. Dedupe rows on run id with `sort -u -k1,1` so one run is rerun once. Submit the non-protect reruns concurrently: `rerun "$id" &` for each row, then a bare `wait`, and only then `rerun "$protect_id"`, so protect is still submitted last, after all other reruns have been submitted.
Symptom: A job that failed on an earlier attempt and then succeeded (or is still pending) on a newer attempt of the same commit was still rerun on approval, and checks outside the PR rollup were considered.
Constraints: Applies only to the approval-triggered rerun workflow. The GraphQL query needs only `actions: write` and works on public repos without extra read permissions. Filters and ordering are unchanged from before; only the source of check data, the superseded-check dedupe, and the submission concurrency changed. Parallel submission does not change the ordering guarantee: protect is submitted only after the `wait` barrier.
applies: Approval-triggered rerun of failed GitHub Actions checks on a PR head SHA; not the general CI workflows.
